sources.fullCitation: “Grand-Montrouge. Grande Rue – Avenue de la République.” Picture postcard, publisher and photographer unidentified, posted at Montrouge before 1931. Archives départementales des Hauts-de-Seine, 9FI/MON_17; digital image via Wikimedia Commons.
sources.title: Grand-Montrouge, Grande Rue – Avenue de la République — postcard
sources.creator: Photographer unidentified
sources.repository: Archives départementales des Hauts-de-Seine / Wikimedia Commons
sources.researchNote: The Commons record dates the card to 1900, a round figure; the card carries a 10-centime Semeuse stamp and a Montrouge postmark, so it was published and posted in the first decades of the century, long before 1931. It shows Montrouge, not the Salabert studio, whose street address has not been established.

media.title: Grand-Montrouge, Grande Rue — postcard, early twentieth century
media.description: Picture postcard of the Grande Rue at the Avenue de la République in Grand-Montrouge, posted in Montrouge in the early twentieth century. It shows the suburb south of Paris where Salabert had its recording studio; the studio itself is not depicted.
media.altText: Sepia postcard of a Montrouge street corner with shops, gas lamps, pedestrians and a stamped postmark in the upper left.
media.publicCaption: Grand-Montrouge, Grande Rue, on a postcard of the early twentieth century — the suburb of Paris where Salabert had its recording studio.
media.publicCreditLine: Postcard, photographer unidentified; Archives départementales des Hauts-de-Seine, 9FI/MON_17; via Wikimedia Commons.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The postcard was published without a photographer’s credit and posted well before 1931, so the French term for an anonymous work has expired and the card is out of copyright in the United States by date. The Archives départementales des Hauts-de-Seine publish the digitisation under the Licence Ouverte, which asks for attribution of the source.

timelineEvents.title: Press report on the Salabert studio in Montrouge
timelineEvents.label: 23 Dec 1933 · Salabert studio report
timelineEvents.shortDescription: A Paris-Soir report placed Kaper and Jurmann at the Salabert studio in Montrouge during a recording session.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Paris-Soir reported that Kaper and Jurmann were present at the Salabert recording studio in Montrouge, where Henri Garat recorded songs for his latest film.

places.publicNote: On 23 December 1933 Paris-Soir reported Kaper and Jurmann at the Salabert recording studio in Montrouge. The studio’s exact street address has not been verified, so the map marker represents Montrouge at city level.
